notes: The input is the bytes of one file. A text input stands for its UTF-8 bytes. A base64 input holds bytes that are no UTF-8 text. A repeat input is a long text.
The entry point is the TOML reader of a file kind, with the kind ROSTER. Its byte limit is 1048576, the largest limit of the four kinds.
An accepted vector is a text that the entry point reads. value is the table that it gives.
A refused vector holds the text of the refusal in refusal. It is one of four fixed texts, and it names no line, no column and no character of the file.

A date-time in value is an object with one key and the value null. The key is the kind of the date-time: offset date-time, local date-time, local date or local time. TOML has no null, so no table of a text has that form. No vector holds a part of the value of a date-time.
A CR LF is one line end. In value, a CR LF inside a multi-line string is one LF. A CR with no LF after it is in no accepted text.
A float that is not finite is a $float marker. The sign of a zero is a part of a float: compare 0.0 and -0.0 as two values.

The vectors changed-000 to changed-499 are changed texts. Each one is an accepted text that a person wrote, with one change: a character less, one more character, two characters swapped, or one line copied to another place. A fixed seed makes them.
